chapter: Back in Houston, Club Ebony and Boo Pleasant
title: Boo's mother kills her father in Corpus Christi in 1954
summary: On the way to open at the Eldorado in August 1954 Boo learns her alcoholic mother shot her father, Corpus Christi's Black politician, and no trial followed.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: When she was with me, her mother killed her daddy in Corpus Christi. We're on our way down to Houston. We

get to Atlanta, Georgia, a long distance called in, and her brother called her. She said, 'Mother killed Daddy.' And she wanted to leave them there. In Atlanta, I said, 'We're going to Jackson, Mississippi. It'd be cheaper for you to go (inaudible). Come on, ride with us. You can't get there any faster. And ain't nothing you can do yet anyway.'

So she run on into Jackson. I got a plane flight out of there for her. It was less money than going from -- come into Corpus Christi where her family were. We come down to open in El Dorado for two weeks with Little Jimmy Scott, August, 1954. And my wife and the guy that drives for me and valet with me, Red, they drove to Corpus Christi and attended the funeral. So she didn't work the first week with me. She worked the second week and brought her brother back, who could play terrific trombone, [Ellick Chaplain. Chapman,]

But what happened was her mother was an alcoholic, and she used to play piano, used to be in the entertainment field, and the old man was a politician. He'd get people out of jail, and he was the Black -- bronze mayor of Corpus Christi. And the police department trusted him and anybody in his care. He was a big man there. He had a liquor store. He had everything operating for him. And he had told them at the liquor store, don't send no whiskey over to his wife.

But she had her contact in the store, and they'd bring it anyway. So finally he come in this thing [went so,] and he put his gun down, said, "If you want to kill me, go on and kill me." He put the gun down. He did it one time too often. He'd been doing it. They'd get into heated arguments about her drinking and then -- and he put the gun down this time, and she picked it up, and she did kill him.

Nothing. You can figure that out for yourself. As a politician and a Black politician in Corpus Christi -- they said good riddance -- too powerful. You know how these things work. She went to California. All blew off. Never went --
What about the little girl. Do you ever hear about her anymore? The little girl --

She's in Jersey. Her mother's in Jersey. She bought a home there (inaudible). She and her mother don't get along one iota. And especially with the daughter, she don't get along. And Boo got another girl. I don't know her. In fact, I've never seen her.
